jobs.title: Equity Institutional Portfolio Manager
jobs.description:
At MFS, you will find a culture that supports you in doing what you do best. Our employees work together to reach better outcomes, favoring the strongest idea over the strongest individual. We put people first and demonstrate care and compassion for our community and each other. Because what we do matters – to us as valued professionals and to the millions of people and institutions who rely on us to help them build more secure and prosperous futures.

THE ROLE
Using discretion and judgment serve as lead portfolio management representative for assigned products to internal and external clients.  For the assigned strategies, take the lead role in strategically managing the business, partnering with distribution on investment-related client service and contributing to alpha generation.  Act as a true investment professional who can credibly stand in for the portfolio managers with major institutional clients and consultants, retail due-diligence teams, large financial advisor audiences, etc.

WHAT YOU WILL DO
- Establish a credible investment-based relationship with the applicable Portfolio Management group; serve as an integral member of the investment team.
- Articulate investment style and portfolio strategy effectively to all audiences. Position the portfolios with consultants, clients and prospects; be able to communicate not only the record, but also the “message.”  Clearly articulate investment strategies and discuss specific holdings.
- Assume primary responsibility for portfolio management functions other than stock selection, including negotiating client guidelines for new accounts, management of cash in clone portfolios, management of customized portfolios (as well as internal and external marketing and client service as mentioned above). Maintain high level of proficiency on portfolio holdings and portfolio positioning by utilizing investment resources (analysts, portfolio managers, company meetings, industry conferences, etc.).
- Work with distribution channels to develop overall, long-term distribution strategy for each product (addressable markets/channels, key competitor analysis, market share and product capacity analysis, product profitability, required resources, etc.).
- Work with PMs to develop/define/refine investment philosophy and style. Develop materials (presentations, white papers) which validate style attributes. Identify and track metrics to monitor consistency of approach. Develop materials to help set appropriate client expectations and retain assets when style is out of favor.
- Provide regular investment updates (quarterly, annual) to distribution groups on performance attribution, significant transactions, and investment outlook.
- Contribute to investment team (as other portfolio managers do) by generating investment ideas, monitoring existing holdings, and managing risk by utilizing internal MFS fundamental and quantitative research, as well as attending company meetings, industry conferences, etc
- Contribute to the firm's sustainability initiatives and communications with clients including providing detailed engagement examples illustrating MFS' integrated approach to material E,S,G issues with companies we invest in.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
- MBA and/or CFA Charterholder preferred.
- Minimum 7-10 experience in the investment management business, work experience as an Institutional Portfolio Manager preferred. Experience working with institutional clients, consultants and managing portfolios preferred.
- Broad knowledge of the investment environment, economic trends, financial markets and competitive trends. In-depth knowledge of the US Equity markets in order to build credibility quickly and forge relationships throughout the organization.
- Strong presentation skills and communication skills, both written and verbal.
- High level of attention to detail; proactive and diligent in responding to business and client needs

Base Salary: $175,000

This position is eligible for competitive incentive bonus.

This range reflects our good-faith expectation for what we’ll pay depending on the candidate’s experience, training and education. jobs.description:

THE ROLE
The Global Fixed Income Institutional Portfolio Manager (IPM) is an integral member of the MFS Fixed Income investment organization.  The role is positioned within portfolio management teams focused on Global Multi-Sector, Global Credit, Global Sovereign, and European-focused public fixed income investment strategies.  The IPM represents these teams in direct engagements with clients, prospects, consultants & gatekeepers, and other marketplace stakeholders worldwide, providing transparency of investment philosophy, process and portfolio strategy.  The IPM also serves as an investment leader for internal MFS colleagues to shape investment narratives, share market insights, communicate portfolio strategy, and serve as a subject matter expert in assisting the execution of strategic initiatives.  Importantly, the IPM also delivers marketplace insights to investment teams and contributes to ongoing enhancement of investment process and overall alignment to client objectives and expectations.  The position is in MFS’ London investment office and will report to the MFS Head of Institutional Fixed Income.

WHAT YOU WILL DO
- Integrate into portfolio management teams with a strong level of credibility and respect
- Represent the voice of the client within investment teams and across the Fixed Income investment organization, ensuring team awareness of client objectives, sharing client feedback, and promoting alignment to highest quality investment standards
- Serve as the primary external marketplace and MFS cross-organizational representative of respective investment teams, providing clarity & depth of investment philosophy, process, portfolio strategy and overall global macroeconomic & asset class insights
- Lead investment team preparation for optimizing client engagements
- Deliver relevant marketplace insights into the Fixed Income investment organization, including important trends, developments, and competitive positioning
- Contribute investment insights and viewpoints as part of portfolio team strategy discussions
- Partner with product and RFP teams to develop and support oversight of investment collateral and to contribute to facilitating client deliverables
- Collaborate across distribution teams to catalyze & promote strategic initiatives and organizational priorities
- Partner organizationally to support development of expanded investment capabilities and strategies
- Support a unified, team-oriented IPM organization focused on the development, execution, and sharing of best practices

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
- Ideally 7+ years of experience communicating, collaborating, and developing strategic relationships with sophisticated institutional asset owners, consultants and gatekeepers
- Robust capability to deliver in-depth transparency for investment process, strategy viewpoints and portfolio positioning, with a refined and flexible ability to contextualize within a global macroeconomic framework
- Multi-dimensional knowledge of global and regional fixed income markets, including delineated rates and credit understanding
- Broad written, verbal and client-facing investment communication skills, with the capability to effectively tailor engagement across a range of investment knowledge and understanding
- Demonstrated history of proactively and effectively engaging across multiple teams of organizational stakeholders in collaborative partnership
- Desire and capability to travel extensively, with a particular focus on Europe and the Americas
- Pan-European language skills very positively viewed

THE ROLE
Using discretion and sound judgment, the Senior Treasury Analyst supports and performs key Treasury functions across cash management, bank administration, financial analysis and the maintenance and enhancement of the Kyriba treasury management system. The role contributes to daily liquidity activities, financial close processes, internal and external reporting, and process improvement initiatives. This position works independently on assigned responsibilities while partnering with department leadership, Corporate Finance, business units, and external service providers to ensure accurate, timely, and efficient Treasury operations.

WHAT YOU WILL DO
- Support global cash management operations in collaboration with the Treasury team for MFS and its subsidiaries: - Determining the daily cash availability and ascertaining if it meets requirements; if requirements aren’t met, proposes solutions to move back into compliance.
- Initiate short-term investments based on daily cash availability
- Reconcile daily cash activity
- Global payment administration
- Utilizing their judgement and expertise to handle day-to-day inquiries and issues that arise

- Creates control reports and financial analysis, related to the following Treasury functions: - Cash forecasting
- Debt management
- Seed investments and derivative positions

- Bank relationship management for the corporate treasury function, including annual audits of authorized signers, oversight of personally identifiable information (PII) held by banks, and coordination of annual tax filings. - Analyzes and makes recommendations for all processes within the department, but specifically regarding the costs and benefits of alternative banking services and products.
- Communicates and resolves all bank service issues with external service providers and relating to financial applications and reports. Additionally, presents and interfaces with internal stakeholders like Corporate Finance or business units.

- Manage and maintain the Kyriba treasury management system - Serve as the MFS liaison with the Kyriba account management team
- Manage and coordinate system updates and enhancements
- Manage and track support tickets and outstanding service issues to be resolved by vendor

- Participate in project teams and make suggestions to result in new and revised procedures and system modifications.
- Assumes additional responsibilities as requested.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
- Bachelor’s degree and 2-5+ years of related Treasury, Finance, Accounting, or cash management experience.
- Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-resolution skills with demonstrated attention to detail.
- Ability to work independently on assigned responsibilities and exercise sound judgment in resolving routine and moderately complex issues.
- Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to interact effectively with internal stakeholders and external banking partners.
- Strong computer skills, including spreadsheet and database applications; familiarity with Treasury Management Systems (Kyriba, G-Treasury, etc.), financial reporting tools, and banking platforms.
- Certified Treasury Professional (CTP) certification preferred.
- Experience with Bloomberg, Treasury Management Systems, bank portals

jobs.description:
At MFS, you will find a culture that supports you in doing what you do best. Our employees work together to reach better outcomes, favoring the strongest idea over the strongest individual. We put people first and demonstrate care and compassion for our community and each other. Because what we do matters – to us as valued professionals and to the millions of people and institutions who rely on us to help them build more secure and prosperous futures.

THE ROLE
Using discretion and judgment, the Senior Compensation Consultant provides advanced compensation expertise, analytics, and consultation to support MFS’s business and talent objectives. Owns complex compensation workstreams or capabilities, translating data, policy, and market insights into clear recommendations and decision-ready guidance. Partners closely with Compensation leadership, HR, Finance, and other stakeholders to ensure compensation programs and practices are effective, consistent, and aligned with MFS’s Compensation Philosophy.

WHAT YOU WILL DO
- Owns and leads complex compensation programs, processes, or functional capabilities (e.g., market data, governance, annual planning, partnering standards), operating independently within established frameworks.

- Applies deep compensation knowledge to evaluate issues, identify risks, and develop practical, value-added solutions aligned with MFS’s Compensation Philosophy.

- Leverages compensation analytics and external market data to assess competitiveness, internal equity, and program effectiveness.

- Interprets data and trends to develop insights, scenarios, and recommendations that inform compensation decisions and planning.

- Provides senior-level consultation to HR partners, Finance, and business stakeholders on compensation matters, including interpretation of guidelines and application of market data.

- Ensures compensation programs and processes are executed with appropriate controls, documentation, and governance to support consistency, auditability, and risk management.

- Continuously evaluates compensation processes, tools, and workflows to improve efficiency, quality, and scalability.

- Leads mid-to-large compensation projects, managing scope, timelines, dependencies, and stakeholder engagement.

- Works collaboratively across the Compensation team, sharing expertise and contributing to broader functional initiatives; may provide informal guidance to more junior team members.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
- Bachelor’s degree in a related area.

- 6–8+ years of experience in compensation, financial analysis or closely related analytical discipline.

- Strong analytical capability with experience using market data and analytics to inform recommendations and decisions.

- Ability to synthesize complex information into clear, actionable recommendations.

- Strong communication, organizational, and stakeholder-management skills.

- Advanced Excel skills, including building and maintaining complex models and analyses

PREFERRED SKILLS, QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE
- Knowledge of compensation regulations, job evaluation, and external benchmarking practices.

- Experience with compensation and HRIS tools (e.g., Workday, MarketPay).

THE ROLE
The Enterprise Risk Officer leads the development, advancement, and continuous improvement of MFS’ enterprise risk framework for Technology and Artificial Intelligence (AI). Serves as the Enterprise Risk subject matter expert for Tech/AI risk assessment and Tech/AI risk mitigation across MFS, ensuring the program effectively meets the needs of the firm and adapts to evolving regulatory expectations.

The role is responsible for helping establish, maintain, and operationalize risk management and governance practices for AI-enabled solutions, machine learning, generative AI, intelligent automation, advanced analytics, and related emerging technologies. Working closely with the MFS AI Governance Group and second-and first-line stakeholders, the incumbent provides effective challenge and practical risk guidance to support responsible AI adoption and resilient technology operations consistent with MFS’ risk appetite, regulatory obligations, and strategic objectives.

WHAT YOU WILL DO
- Tech & AI Risk Program Leadership and Implementation: Lead the design and operational execution of MFS’ Technology and AI Risk program, ensuring it meets business objectives, aligns to global standards, and adapts to emerging threats, business change, and regulatory updates.

- AI Governance Program Implementation and Operation: Partner with, and provide second-line support to, the MFS AI Governance Group to operationalize the firm’s AI governance framework.

- Support intake, review, approval, and ongoing monitoring processes for AI tools and use cases (generative AI, algorithmic AI, and agentic solutions).

- AI Risk Assessment and Mitigation: Conduct and facilitate risk assessments for AI, generative AI, machine learning, intelligent automation, and advanced analytics.

- Assess risks related to transparency, explainability, reliability, bias, fairness, privacy, data quality, security, resilience, human oversight, and third-party dependency.

- Develop practical risk mitigation recommendations, monitor action plans through completion, and escalate significant risks, issues, and control gaps through appropriate governance channels.

- Technology and Emerging Technology Risk Oversight: Assess technology risks arising from the integration of new tools with legacy systems, cloud and platform adoption, and the modernization of core infrastructure, coordinating with GIT, Information Security, and Data Governance.

- Controls, Monitoring, and Reporting: Evaluate the design and effectiveness of Tech and AI-related governance controls, key risk indicators, monitoring routines, and documentation practices; support the development of risk metrics, dashboards, and reporting for senior management and governance committees.

- Third-Party and Vendor Technology/AI Risk: Partner with third-party risk and business owners to assess concentration, operational, cyber, contractual, and resilience risks associated with technology and AI vendors, including fourth-party dependencies.

- Change and Transformation Risk Assessments: Lead or support targeted risk assessments for significant technology, data-driven, AI-enabled, and transformation initiatives, evaluating impacts on governance, controls, data, process ownership, and operational resilience.

- Risk Culture, Training, and Stakeholder Engagement: Facilitate workshops and training to advance the organization’s understanding of responsible AI and technology risk, and build trusted relationships across Risk, Technology, Compliance, Legal, Information Security, Data Governance, and the business.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience.

- 8-12+ years of relevant work experience in risk (enterprise, operational, technology, or IT risk), investment management, financial services, or technology.

- Demonstrated knowledge of AI governance, AI risk management, machine learning, generative AI, intelligent automation, advanced analytics, model governance, data governance, and emerging technology risk.

- Demonstrated experience with global technology and operational resilience regulations, e.g., DORA and UK Operational Resilience, and evolving AI regulatory frameworks and best practices.

- Ability to assess AI and technology risks and translate technical and emerging technology risks into practical business, control, and governance considerations for senior stakeholders.

- Strong analytical skills, with a proven ability to work independently and synthesize complex information.

- Strong project management and organizational skills, including the ability to complete projects and reports within communicated deadlines.

- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, capable of working with all levels of management and collaboratively across team and departmental boundaries.

- Some periodic travel, domestic and international, may be required.

- In-depth knowledge and hands-on experience using Archer GRC preferred.

PREFERRED SKILLS, QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE
- Experience implementing, operating, or independently reviewing AI governance or responsible AI programs, including AI use case intake, AI vendor risk, and AI control design.

- Experience with Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) platforms, workflow tools, risk analytics, and data visualization tools such as Tableau or Power BI.

- Understanding of information security, third-party risk, model risk, SOX, COSO, and operational resilience requirements.

- Experience within investment management or asset management.
